summary: Implemented asynchronous click analytics queue with Celery and Redis broker, hot path redirect decoupling, idempotent worker consumption, 30-day retention cleanup, and owner-scoped analytics endpoint.
evidence: Decoupled click analytics from redirect hot path in apps/api/app/routers/redirect.py: HTTP 307 returned immediately without awaiting database write
Configured Celery worker in apps/api/app/celery_app.py and app/worker.py connected to Redis broker (redis://localhost:6379/0)
Applied additive database migration adding click_event_id VARCHAR(64) UNIQUE index to click_events table
Enforced idempotency in record_click_event_task using PostgreSQL ON CONFLICT (click_event_id) DO NOTHING RETURNING id
Enforced privacy protection: hashed client IP via SHA-256 (ip_hash); raw client IP is never transmitted in queue payload or stored in database
Implemented queue-down resilience drill: verified HTTP 307 redirect succeeds without hanging or 500 error when queue enqueue fails
Implemented protected owner-scoped GET /links/{id}/analytics with date range filtering, ISO date validation, and 404 for cross-tenant access
Implemented purge_expired_clicks_task with 30-day retention window purging expired clicks while preserving active links and recent records
Executed apps/api/verify_module_07.py: 10/10 tests passed including live Celery worker consumption from Redis
Executed regression test suites: verify_module_06.py (6/6 passed) and verify_module_05.py (9/9 passed) with 0 regressions
Preserved PostgreSQL database upsk_sdf and Docker containers upsk-sdf-postgres and bootcamp-redis with 0 data loss
